newsitem.title: UK: London palladium fixes at fresh high of $135.00.
newsitem.headline: London palladium fixes at fresh high of $135.00.

text.p: Palladium fixed at its highest level since May 8, 1996 on Tuesday passing its previous recent high of $134.25 struck on Monday.
Dealers said fund buying on top of consumer covering against tightness, caused by the delayed Russia-Japan 1997 supply contract, was behind the rise.
Palladium prices have been climbing since they slumped to around three and a half year lows in late November last year at around $114.00.
Heavier that usual Russsian shipments to the United States and Switzerland, a major user and major trader respectively in the metals pressured the price at that time.
Dealers and analysts said that after working off excessive inventories last year, palladium users in major consumer Japan were looking to expand offtake again this year.
Palladium is used in electronic components, dental alloys, many chemical industry applications and in autocatalysts for removing toxic gases from car exhaust.
